summary: API gateway connection imbalance causing cascading runtime panics and elevated 5xx rate
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC customers reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503/504) for conversational endpoints for the Converso Labs tenant. Impact: ~12% global request error rate for the tenant, multiple streaming sessions dropped, and customer reports degraded UX and retries. Environment: prod:us-east (dedicated cluster), serving-runtime v2.7.1, api-gateway v1.12.

Observed behavior:
- Rapid increase in accept-queue depth on front-line API gateway nodes servicing the tenant.
- Long-lived HTTP/1.1 keepalive connections from a subset of Converso clients (long polling) created backlog in gateway accept queue and caused connection fanout imbalance.
- Gateway began serializing handoffs to runtimes; runtimes experienced thread-pool saturation leading to OOM-like panic traces and clean process restarts.
- Downstream effect: API gateway returning 502/503/504 while runtimes cycled; internal autoscaler triggered ephemeral warm-ups that amplified the wave.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Simulated tenant traffic with a mix of short chat requests and a minority (~8%) of long-polling websocket/keepalive connections.
2) Gradually increased long-polling clients; once accept-queue exceeded 85% the gateway started handoff serialization.
3) Runtimes reported sustained threadpool queue growth and occasional panic stacks referencing epoll_wait + uvloop.

Logs and metrics:
- apigw/accept_queue_depth spiked from baseline ~30 to 120+ for the tenant shard between 02:10-02:20 UTC.
- runtime/thread_pool_queue_len increased to 700+ and per-routine latency jumped.
- kernel logs include repeated 'epoll_wait woke too many fds' warnings and runtime traces referencing 'thread pool exhaustion -> panic: runtime: out of memory?'.
- No single large payloads were observed; average payload size remained under 1.2KB.

Expected behavior: Gateway should load-balance handoffs without causing runtime thread-pool saturation; runtimes should throttle or shed connections gracefully rather than panicking.
comments: 2026-03-12 02:28 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports intermittent 5xx on chat endpoints. Collected logs and suggested immediate mitigation: apply tenant rate-limit and enable connection-cull on apigw nodes for Converso tenant. Escalated to SRE.

2026-03-12 03:05 UTC - SRE (Diego Ramos): Confirmed accept_queue spike on two apigw nodes. Applied temporary ingress rate-limit (converso-longpoll: 20rps) and enabled aggressive keepalive cull; error rate dropped from 12% to 4% within 6 minutes. Noted runtime thread pool still elevated; investigating handoff pattern.

2026-03-12 04:10 UTC - Eng (Priya Nair): Found stack traces referencing uvloop/epoll_wait wake storm in runtime logs. Hypothesis: a combination of long-lived half-open sockets + apigw handoff serialization created high epoll churn, causing runtime thread contention and eventual panic. Preparing patch to change handoff path to non-blocking async accept and increase runtime backpressure signals.

2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Customer (Converso Ops): Confirmed UX improved after temporary limits; asked for ETA on a permanent fix and whether this could recur during weekend traffic patterns. Requested a postmortem and knob to prevent recurrence without dropping long-poll clients.

2026-03-14 11:30 UTC - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Deployed hotfix to apigw handoff to use non-blocking socket transfers and added an upstream 'soft-shed' signal for runtimes. Monitoring shows accept_queue back to baseline and thread_pool_queue_len reduced to normal. Scheduling postmortem and follow-up load-test to validate with mixed long-poll ratio.
investigation_notes: Correlated apigw accept-queue spikes with a subset of long-poll clients that keep connections open but remain idle for long periods. The gateway's handoff path used a synchronous accept/handoff that serialized on busy nodes; this created uneven distribution to runtimes and created epoll wake storms in uvloop-based runtimes. Autoscaler warm-ups and ephemeral worker churn amplified the issue. Reproduced locally with a long-poll ratio ~8-10% and keepalive interval disabled on simulated clients.
mitigation: Temporary: Applied tenant-scoped ingress rate limits for long-poll connections and enabled keepalive culling on affected apigw nodes. Permanent/En route: apigw handoff hotfix (non-blocking transfer) deployed 2026-03-14; runtime 'soft-shed' signal added to shed low-priority connections when thread pool exceeds threshold.
resolution: Mitigated - hotfix deployed to apigw and runtime soft-shed implemented. Error rate for Converso Labs tenant reduced to baseline (~0.8%). Root cause: synchronous handoff path + long-poll client mix causing epoll wake/thread saturation and runtime panics. Pending full postmortem and load-test validation.
follow_up_actions: Run mixed-traffic load test with 0-15% long-poll clients to verify resilience
Add tenant-level long-poll detection and adaptive soft-shed policy in autoscaler
Postmortem write-up and update runbook: ingress-accept-queue and keepalive knobs
Customer follow-up: provide mitigation summary and timeline for permanent fixes
